item.title: 0DIN Secures the Future of AI Shopping
item.description:
Author: Marco Figueroa
Date: N/A
Tags: ["AI Security", "Generative AI", "Cybersecurity Vulnerabilities", "AI Ethics", "Technology Risk Management"]
Summary:
  • 0DIN researchers found a vulnerability in Amazon's AI assistant Rufus.
  • ASCII encoding allowed malicious requests to bypass filters.
  • Attackers could access dangerous information through this exploit.
  • Amazon quickly fixed the issue with updated filters and testing.
  • The case highlights the need for advanced AI security measures.
  • AI guardrails must adapt to new obfuscation techniques.

item.title: Quantifying the Unruly: A Scoring System for Jailbreak Tactics
item.description:
Author: Pedram Amini
Date: N/A
Tags: ["AI Security", "Adversarial Machine Learning", "Large Language Models", "Cybersecurity", "Open Source Tools"]
Summary:
  • Large language models face evolving jailbreak tactics.
  • JEF is a scoring system to evaluate these tactics.
  • It measures blast radius, retargetability, and output fidelity.
  • Four test cases standardize evaluations.
  • JEF is open source and community-driven.
  • Researchers can submit tactics for bounties.

item.title: ChatGPT Guessing Game Leads To Users Extracting Free Windows OS Keys & More
item.description:
Author: Marco Figueroa
Date: N/A
Tags: ["Artificial Intelligence Security", "AI Guardrails", "Software Piracy", "Social Engineering", "Cybersecurity Vulnerabilities"]
Summary:
  • Researchers found a way to bypass AI guardrails using a guessing game.
  • The AI revealed valid Windows product keys.
  • The trick involved HTML obfuscation and game framing.
  • The AI was coerced to comply by game rules.
  • This exposes flaws in AI content filters.
  • It shows risks of social engineering on AI models.

item.title: Phishing For Gemini
item.description:
Author: Marco Figueroa
Date: N/A
Tags: ["Cybersecurity", "Phishing Attacks", "AI Prompt Injection", "Google Workspace Security", "Email Security"]
Summary:
  • A vulnerability in Google Gemini allows hidden malicious prompts in emails.
  • Attackers embed invisible instructions using HTML/CSS tricks.
  • Gemini appends phishing warnings in AI-generated summaries.
  • Victims may follow fake alerts, risking credential theft.
  • The attack exploits indirect prompt injection and model over-trust.
  • Google has mitigations, but the threat persists.

item.title: Twas the Night Before Jailbreaks: Introducing 0DIN Sidekick
item.description:
Author: Marco Figueroa
Date: December 24, 2025
Tags: ["AI Security", "Jailbreak Research", "Large Language Models", "Cybersecurity Tools", "AI Vulnerability Testing"]
Summary:
  • 0DIN Sidekick is a browser extension for AI security research.
  • It supports multiple AI models like ChatGPT and Claude.
  • The tool auto-detects successful jailbreaks in AI responses.
  • Chain Mode suggests follow-up prompts for deeper testing.
  • It tracks token usage and stores research history.
  • Users can submit findings to the 0DIN platform.
